what: How big can the data be?
title: Getting started with Atlas
text: Rows cheap; columns limit matters. Rows: bounded machine, LLM. data never uploaded, printed tool output capped (~8,000 characters per chunk), million rows cost fitting time, tokens. Columns: double digits ideal, low hundreds practical ceiling. agent reasons variables name; data profile lists 50 columns. wide data — one-hot blocks, text features, omics — pre-select first, tell goal (“variance filter, work top 30”). Cost scales agent steps. candidates, repair rounds, follow-ups mean LLM calls; rows don’t. typical build dozen calls. Disk: run directory keeps copy data sessions resume cold. Point dir (options(atlas.dir = )) somewhere room large datasets.

what: Three ways to write a constraint
title: Domain knowledge and constraints
text: Prefer check whenever rule testable; reserve strings rules agent can honour. check may also stop() — errors count violations, error message detail.
code: library(atlas)  res <- atlas(mtcars, "mpg", n_models = 2, constraints = list(   # 1. built-in helpers: machine-checked, model-agnostic   uses_wt = con_uses("wt"),   mono_hp = con_monotone("hp", "decreasing"),    # 2. custom check: function(model, data) -> TRUE or a violation message   non_neg = constraint(     "predicted mpg must never be negative",     check = function(model, data) {       p <- predict(model, newdata = data)       if (all(p >= 0)) TRUE else "some predictions are negative"     }   ),    # 3. plain string: enforced via instructions only   no_leak = "qsec is measured after the fact; never use it as a predictor" ))

title: Domain knowledge and constraints
text: helpers model-agnostic: need predict(model, newdata = <data.frame>) work, Atlas tells agent every final model must support exactly . con_uses(var) asserts model actually uses variable. check scrambles column compares predictions: don’t move, variable isn’t contributing. formula inspection, works identically glm, random forest, wrapped model object. con_monotone(var, direction) asserts predictions monotone variable, ICE-style: sample observed rows, variable swept across range everything else held fixed, every step must move stated direction (within tol). Monotonicity non-strict, feature: model ignores variable flat — hence monotone — response, passes. con_monotone() alone means “model responds hp, effect must decreasing”. Pair con_uses() also force variable :
code: # conditional: monotone if used, but may be dropped constraints = list(mono_hp = con_monotone("hp", "decreasing"))  # mandatory and monotone constraints = list(uses_hp = con_uses("hp"),                    mono_hp = con_monotone("hp", "decreasing"))

title: Domain knowledge and constraints
text: property can compute (model, data) can guarantee:
code: # a performance floor min_r2 <- constraint(   "in-sample R-squared must be at least 0.7",   check = function(model, data) {     r2 <- cor(predict(model, newdata = data), data$mpg)^2     if (r2 >= 0.7) TRUE else sprintf("R-squared is %.2f", r2)   } )  # bounded predictions in_range <- constraint(   "predictions must stay within the observed outcome range",   check = function(model, data) {     p <- predict(model, newdata = data)     if (all(p >= min(data$mpg) & p <= max(data$mpg))) TRUE     else "predictions leave the observed range"   } )  # parity across a group fair_gap <- constraint(   "mean absolute error must be within 1 unit across am groups",   check = function(model, data) {     err <- abs(data$mpg - predict(model, newdata = data))     gap <- abs(diff(tapply(err, data$am, mean)))     if (gap <= 1) TRUE else sprintf("MAE gap across am is %.2f", gap)   } )

title: Domain knowledge and constraints
text: extract_constraints() turns plain-language brief constraint objects, mapping machine checks wherever recognises checkable rule: Parsing intent judgment call, function returns list inspect edit rather feeding straight build. Pass data validate column names; anything unmappable (unknown column, monotone rule without direction) falls back prompt-enforcement instead becoming broken check.
code: cons <- extract_constraints(   "weight must be in the model; predictions can never go up as horsepower    rises; qsec is measured after the fact, never use it",   data = mtcars ) cons #> $uses_wt #> [machine-checked] The variable `wt` must be used as a predictor. #> $mono_hp #> [machine-checked] Predictions must be monotonically decreasing in `hp`. #> $no_qsec #> [prompt-only]     Never use qsec as a predictor.  res <- atlas(mtcars, "mpg", constraints = cons)

title: atlas — automated model building with LLM agents

Give data frame target; LLM agent (via ellmer) explores data, proposes modeling plan approval, writes runs R code fit, compare, refine candidate models. get back fitted models ready predict(), leaderboard, written report — , agent works writing R, complete script everything . NULL (default), questions asked console (interactive sessions) answered "use best judgment" (scripts). Used atlas_app() route questions browser. display verbose progress formatted: "console" (cli rules colours) "markdown" (fenced code blocks, front-ends render stream markdown, like atlas_app()). stopping_rounds Stopping rule: give iteration (adding candidates, refinement loop) many consecutive attempts without improvement. stopping_tolerance Stopping rule: attempt counts improvement beats best validation metric far least relative fraction, 0 1 (e.g. 0.05 5%). exclude Columns models must use (available prediction time, leakage). removed data agent ever sees - strongest possible guarantee. interject Optional function() polled every tool call. Return string interrupt agent message mid-build (delivered next tool result, marked highest priority); return NULL nothing say. Used atlas_app()'s "Send now" box; front-ends typically read message file queue. autonomous Run without human: agent states plan proceeds instead asking approval, never calls ask_user. test_prop Proportion rows (0 <1) hold final test set agent never sees. Final models evaluated Atlas run ($results()$test_leaderboard), comparison gamed overfitting agent's validation scheme. 0 (default) disables split. compact_at Token budget conversation. context grows past many input tokens, compacted next message: transcript archived run directory, window cleared, agent re-oriented briefing built session state (extra LLM call). Long runs stay inside model's context window stop paying re-read history. Set Inf disable. max_steps Hard budget: maximum number code executions agent gets session. Unlike stopping rules (agent applies ), mechanically enforced — past limit run_r_code tool refuses execute instructs agent finalise . Inf (default) disables. max_runtime Hard budget: wall-clock seconds session process, enforced way max_steps. Timing restarts atlas_resume(). Inf (default) disables.

title: Atlas 0.1.0
text: Initial release. atlas() builds n_models candidate models LLM agent: distribution-driven planning, plan approval, held-comparison, feature refinement winner, written report. Stopping controlled patience min_improve. Domain knowledge enforced constraints: constraint(), con_uses(), con_monotone(), natural-language extraction via extract_constraints(), automatic repair rounds, compliance table results. Feature safety: exclude removes columns agent sees data; atlas_leakage_screen() flags predictors alone explain almost outcome. Persistent sessions: AtlasSession checkpoints every code chunk conversation turn run directory; atlas_resume() reconstructs session exactly replaying code log. Builds can interrupted steered mid-run (interject). Optional extras: point--click front-end (atlas_app(), requires ‘shiny’) validation workup winning model (requires ‘modelblueprint’).
